To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of a virtual workspace is an effective way to improve the user’s quality of life in a Grid environment.

1) the quality of service (QoS) provided to the user by a Grid-enabled application depends on the quality of the Grid middleware, 2) the quality of the middleware depends on how it was developed, 3) the quality of Grid middleware development depends on the quality assurance (QA) processes used, 4) the quality of QA depends on the QA processes used, and 5) the quality of these processes depends on the maturity of the QA process model.
the virtual workspace paradigm can be implemented in the Grid, but that the Grid must be extended to provide the necessary quality of service (QoS) guarantees.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and evaluation of a new class of middleware that will enable the construction and management of large-scale virtual workspaces that can be used by users to access and manage Grid resources.

the design and implementation of a Grid middleware that enables the creation and management of virtual workspaces that are dynamically configured and customized for individual users, and that can adapt their configurations in response to changes in user preferences, application requirements, or resource availability.
the development of Grid-enabled, virtual workspaces, which provide users with a high-quality of service (QoS) and quality of life (QoL).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Grids are not a solution for all problems, but they can be a very good solution for many problems.
the grid computing technology is the best solution for the future of the IT industry and that the grid computing is a technology that will be used in the future.
the Grid is not a single technology, but rather a set of technologies and standards that are used to create a virtual workspaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an architecture that provides a quality-of-service (QoS) guarantee for the virtual workspaces in Grid environments.
the Grid is a virtual workspace, and that the Grid middleware should provide a quality of service and a quality of life.
we are developing a framework for the design, deployment, and management of virtual workspaces that are capable of meeting quality of service (QoS) requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Grid community should not only focus on the development of Grid middleware and services, but also on the development of a Grid culture that promotes and supports a new way of working.

the Grid can be used to provide users with a virtual workspace, a place in which they can access the resources they need to do their work and where they can be assured that these resources meet their quality of service requirements.
the quality of service in the Grid is not a technical issue, but a social one, and that it is the users who must take the responsibility for ensuring the quality of their own work [1].
